data.narrative:
Astroscale, a publicly traded Space & Aerospace company founded by Mitsunobu Okada, has raised $400M+ and currently trades at an $840M valuation. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of 4 same-sector, same-stage comparables: SpaceX ($1.6T), Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B).

Peer-median valuation methodology applies here as the sole applicable triangulation method. The median valuation across the four public Space & Aerospace peers is $23.8B, with a range spanning $2.9B to $1.6T. This wide dispersion reflects the nascent maturity of the sector and substantial heterogeneity in business model and scale among participants. Public-comp anchoring using sector P/S multiples (24.4x median across 6 public tickers including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, and SATL) cannot be applied, as Astroscale's revenue is not on file.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20.2B (low) to $27.3B (high), centered at $23.8B median. This range sits substantially above Astroscale's current $840M trading valuation, suggesting either underpricing relative to peer multiples or divergent investor assessment of the company's competitive positioning and addressable market within in-orbit services. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, profitability path, and the durability of peer valuations given the sector's early commercialization stage.
